name: Weißenbach am Lech
kurzbeschreibung: Welcome to a friendly community in the Lechtal valley, home to the Naturpark Tiroler Lech and a riverside swimming area.
beschreibung:
Überblick

The municipality of Weißenbach am Lech is situated at an elevation of 886 metres above sea level in the Tyrolean Lech Valley within the Reutte district, lying at the confluence where the Weißenbach and Rotlech torrents join the untamed wild River Lech. With approximately 1,300 residents, this delightful village acts as the western gateway to the Tannheimer Tal, sheltered between the Lechtal Alps and the Allgäu Alps. The municipal area forms an integral part of the Nature Park Tiroler Lech, which safeguards one of the last pristine braided wild-river corridors in the Alps with expansive gravel banks and riparian forests. Weißenbach blends serene alpine relaxation, crystal-clear swimming lakes, and diverse mountain sports within an unspoilt natural landscape of the Außerfern.

Geschichte

Its strategic location between the Lech Valley and the Tannheimer Tal has defined Weißenbach since classical antiquity: Roman burial findings along the Via Decia indicate an early role along historic trade routes. The village was first documented in 1200. For centuries, the 1,093-metre Gaichtpass functioned as a crucial section of the Tyrolean Salt Road, along which 'white gold' extracted from Hall in Tirol was transported across the Außerfern towards Lake Constance and Switzerland; fortified salt storehouses at the pass sheltered pack-horse drivers during inclement weather. Furthermore, generations of locals subsisted through timber rafting on the River Lech, shipping logs downriver towards Augsburg. The Baroque parish church of Saint Sebastian was constructed between 1734 and 1738 incorporating a late-Gothic choir tower base.

Anreise

Weißenbach am Lech is conveniently connected to the regional road network. Motorists travelling from Germany can drive toll-free via federal highway B179 through the Füssen border tunnel into Reutte, continuing directly along the Lechtal federal road B198 into Weißenbach. From Innsbruck, drivers travel via the Inntal Autobahn A12 and the Fernpass road B179. In addition, the Tannheimer federal road B199 branches off in Weißenbach, ascending across the Gaichtpass into the Tannheimer Tal. Rail passengers travel via the Außerfernbahn line to Reutte in Tirol railway station. From the station forecourt, regular VVT regional bus services (line 110 towards the Lechtal and line 120 towards Tannheim) provide seamless connections directly to Weißenbach centre.

Tipps

A prime summer attraction is the Weißenbach bathing lake (Lechausee), a peaceful, spring-fed natural swimming lake nestled within riverbank woods that offers crystal-clear water, sunbathing lawns, and swimming against a splendid mountain backdrop. Long-distance hikers on the renowned Lechweg trail cross the historic Johannesbrücke bridge with its statue of Saint John of Nepomuk directly beside the lake, experiencing magnificent vistas of braided gravel channels within the nature park. Heritage enthusiasts should explore the historic pack-horse trail across the Gaichtpass, which offers panoramic views of the Allgäu and Lechtal Alps. Additionally, the scenic Lech Cycle Path provides gentle riverside riding for families.
